concepts.def: The belief in one God in three persons - Father, Son and Holy Spirit - equal, eternal and of one substance.
The belief that God became human in Jesus, fully God and fully man, 'the Word made flesh' (John 1:14).
Jesus died on the cross and, Christians believe, rose on the third day; the resurrection is the foundation of Christian hope.
The belief that Jesus's death restores the broken relationship between God and humanity, dealing with the problem of sin.
Christians teach that salvation comes through God's grace - an undeserved gift of love received through faith rather than earned by works alone.
Christian beliefs about the last things: resurrection of the dead, divine judgement, and the destinations of heaven and hell.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christianity: Beliefs & Teachings — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Christianity: Beliefs & Teachings brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Christianity: Beliefs & Teachings.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: One God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit
Three separate gods working together
Three names God uses at different times in history
The Father, the Son and the Virgin Mary
God became human in Jesus
Jesus's baptism in the Jordan
The ascension of Jesus into heaven
The conversion of Paul

mcqs.q: According to the creeds, on which day did Jesus rise from the dead?
options: The third day
The same day he died
The seventh day
The fortieth day
The reconciliation of God and humanity through Jesus's death
The forty days of Lent
The building of the first churches
The writing of the gospels

mcqs.q: Does the Trinity mean Christians worship three gods?
options: The Trinity means Christians believe in three different gods.
Christians believe Jesus rose as an angel with wings.
The Trinity refers to the three wise men at Jesus's birth.
No - Christianity is monotheist: the Trinity is one God in three persons, and belief in three separate gods (tritheism) is rejected as heresy.

mcqs.q: Do Christians believe Jesus rose only as a ghost or spirit?
options: Christians believe Jesus rose as an angel with wings.
Christians believe heaven is only for clergy.
No - mainstream teaching holds Jesus rose bodily: Luke 24 stresses that he ate food and could be touched, though his risen body was transformed and glorified.
The resurrection means Jesus's ghost appeared to the disciples.

mcqs.q: Do Christians teach that being nice automatically earns heaven?
options: No - salvation is taught as God's gift of grace received through faith, with good works flowing from it; denominations differ on details, but 'earning heaven by niceness' misstates the doctrine.
The Trinity refers to the three wise men at Jesus's birth.
Christians believe heaven is only for clergy.
Christianity teaches that anyone who is kind enough earns a place in heaven.

sequence.def: God makes the world; humans bear God's image
Sin enters through Adam and Eve's disobedience
God becomes human in Jesus, born of Mary
Jesus dies as atonement for sin
Jesus rises and returns to the Father
Christ judges all; heaven or hell follows
